exposure: Uterine fibromyoma (including submucous fibroma and multiple fibromyomas)
cohort: The study included 200 females with singleton pregnancies who had a confirmed diagnosis of uterine fibromyoma and visited the Institutes within the defined study period.
finding: Uterine fibromyomas, specifically submucous and multiple types, were significantly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including spontaneous abortion, PPROM, PROM, preterm delivery, malpresentation, and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: LSCS was performed in 56% and normal vaginal delivery in 36% of subjects, with the study concluding that elective cesarean section is not compulsory unless there are clear obstetrical indications.
